answer.rationale: With the contract expiring in 14 days and the line running at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer, any action that risks delivery continuity (e.g., switching primary vendor to the low-cost supplier that missed SLA in 3 of 4 quarters per memory_c2) is too risky right now. Memory_c4 shows that renegotiating at renewal, benchmarked against market rates, recovered real margin and improved payment terms without disrupting the incumbent relationship—directly addressing the 18% spend-cut mandate while memory_c1 confirms incumbent renewals have kept integration stable with no delivery interruption. I want to verify c4's actual magnitude of savings and c2's SLA miss details before committing, since c4 is the basis for believing negotiation can meet the cost target, and c2 is the strongest counter-argument against a vendor switch that could otherwise look cost-attractive. Given the volume buffer is already gone, avoiding any risk of a supply gap or onboarding hiccup during a 14-day window outweighs the theoretical extra savings from switching vendors. This defers the second-source and full vendor-switch questions to next cycle, consistent with having capacity for only one decision now.
